name: Troy
note: Dardanos to Priam, and the branch through Anchises that leaves for Italy

Dardanos.note: Founder of the line; the DARDANELLES keep his name, as does Homer's Dardanian for the Trojans. Il. 20.215-218

people.Erichthonios: Son of Dardanos, richest of mortal men, with three thousand mares in the marsh. Not Erichthonios of Athens. Il. 20.219-230
people.Tros: King who gave the city and the people their name: TROY, Trojan. Il. 20.230-231
people.Ilos: Son of Tros, founder of Ilion -- the city's other name, and the one the ILIAD is titled from. Il. 20.231-232
people.Assarakos: Son of Tros, and the branch that leaves for Italy. Il. 20.232-233
people.Ganymedes: Most beautiful of mortals, carried up by Zeus' eagle to pour the gods' wine, his father paid in immortal horses. Gives catamite, through Etruscan Catmite and Latin catamitus -- his name, worn down. The moon of Jupiter is his. Il. 20.232-235 Zeus took him for himself -- the clearest statement of the practice in the whole tradition, and the reason his name became the Latin word for it.
people.Laomedon: King who hired Poseidon and Apollo to build his walls and then refused to pay them, and cheated Herakles of the horses owed for saving his daughter -- so Herakles sacked Troy a generation before the Greeks did. Il. 21.441-457, Apollod. 2.5.9

Priamos.name: Priamos (Priam)
Priamos.note: Last king of Troy, spared as a boy when Herakles took the city -- his name was said to mean 'the bought one'. Fifty sons, and he crossed the Greek lines alone at night to kiss the hands of the man who killed the best of them. Il. 24.468-676

Hesione.note: Daughter of Laomedon, given to Telamon after the first sack; mother of Teukros. Apollod. 2.6.4

Hekabe.name: Hekabe (Hecuba)
Hekabe.note: Queen of Troy, who dreamed she gave birth to a firebrand before Paris was born. She lives to see the city burn and every child dead. Euripides Trojan Women; Apollod. 3.12.5

Hektor.name: Hektor (Hector)
Hektor.note: Troy's best, and the most humane figure in the Iliad -- the scene with his wife and the baby frightened of his helmet is the poem's still point. Killed by Achilles and dragged behind his chariot. Il. 6.390-502, 22

Paris.name: Paris (Alexandros)
Paris.note: Exposed as a baby for the firebrand dream, raised as a herdsman, and asked to judge which goddess was fairest. He took Aphrodite's bribe, which was Helen. Killed Achilles with an arrow to the heel, and was a poor fighter otherwise. Apollod. 3.12.5-6, Epit. 3.1-2

Kassandra.note: Given prophecy by Apollo for a promise she then refused, so he spat in her mouth and left her true and disbelieved -- the exact shape of the curse. Taken by Agamemnon and killed with him. Aeschylus Ag. 1072-1330

Deiphobos.note: Son of Priam, who married Helen after Paris died and was cut to pieces on the last night. Aen. 6.494-534

Polyxene.note: Daughter of Priam, sacrificed on Achilles' tomb after the city fell. Euripides Hecuba

Helenos.note: Son of Priam and a seer; he went over to the Greeks and told them the conditions for taking the city. Apollod. Epit. 5.9-10

Troilos.note: Youngest son of Priam, killed young by Achilles; the medieval Troilus-and-Cressida story is built on the name and almost nothing else. Apollod. 3.12.5

Andromache.note: Hektor's wife, who lost her father and seven brothers to Achilles in one day and then her husband and her son; given to Neoptolemos afterwards. Il. 6.390-502

Astyanax.note: Hektor's baby son, thrown from the walls when the city fell so that no heir should grow up. Apollod. Epit. 5.23

people.Anchises: Loved by Aphrodite, who came to him as a mortal girl on Ida and told him afterwards what she was; lamed or blinded by the thunderbolt for boasting of it. Carried out of Troy on his son's shoulders. Hom. Hymn Aphr.; Aen. 2.634-729
people.Tithonos: Brother of Priam, loved by Eos, who begged Zeus to make him immortal and forgot to ask for youth. He shrank and withered and babbled until she shut him in a room, and at last he turned into the CICADA -- which is why it sings all summer and never dies. Hom. Hymn Aphr. 218-238

Memnon.note: Son of Eos and Tithonos, king of the Ethiopians, who brought an army to Troy after Hektor died and killed Antilochos. Achilles killed him, and his mother's tears for him are the morning dew. Apollod. Epit. 5.3

Kreousa.note: Daughter of Priam and Aeneas' first wife, lost in the burning of Troy; her ghost meets him in the street and tells him to go without her. Aen. 2.735-794

unions.note: Elektra is a Pleiad and Dardanos the first Trojan; the Trojan king-list that follows is a bare succession of names, so the shortfall sits at its head.
Nineteen children of one mother, Homer says, out of fifty sons in all. Il. 24.495-497
The mother is Aphrodite; her bond to Anchises is drawn across the eras beside this. Hom. Hymn Aphr. 45-291
The abduction, or the elopement -- the sources are not agreed and Homer lets Helen call it both within a hundred lines. Apollod. Epit. 3.3
Eos' bond to him is drawn across the eras beside this. Apollod. Epit. 5.3
Mother of Dardanos, and so of Troy. Apollod. 3.12.1
The eagle took him off the mountain, and his father was paid afterwards in immortal horses. Il. 20.232-235
She came to him on Ida as a mortal girl and told him afterwards what she was; he was lamed by the thunderbolt for boasting of it. Hom. Hymn Aphr. 45-291
Dawn carried him off, then begged Zeus for his immortality and forgot to ask for his youth. Hom. Hymn Aphr. 218-238
